item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-8fb2179f960886b0","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A 2026 scholarly article describes Sisi’s 2019–2025 Gaza-border policy as combining Rafah border security, humanitarian-aid management, counterterrorism in Sinai, conflict mediation, and regional-leadership objectives, while identifying security discourse as legitimizing domestic practices.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","3B.5","8B.1"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Partially fits 2023 because the study covers 2019–2025; its abstract does not isolate 2023 events.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the policy to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.","limitations":["Abstract-level evidence only; no specific 2023 event, budget, implementation record, or outcome is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cd0d78a389f5df8d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The EU’s 21 August 2013 political commitment suspended licences for Egyptian equipment potentially usable for internal repression and called for reassessment of military-export licences and security assistance after Egyptian security forces killed hundreds; the measures remained formally unrepealed but became unclear, while EU states later supplied significant arms and signed further contracts.","question_ids":["2B.5","3B.2","3B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical context relevant to 2023; the source was last updated in 2017 and does not report 2023 conduct.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes measures directed at Egypt during Sisi’s post-2013 rule but does not attribute the EU decisions personally to Sisi.","limitations":["No 2023 arms-transfer decision or Sisi directive is reported."]},{"source_id":"SRC-102ebc198d82382b","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"An ECFR event description states that Sisi launched a massive military campaign in Sinai against ISIS, but promised results were largely not delivered; the campaign brought harsher laws, closure of political space, destabilization, and destruction affecting local communities.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","4B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical assessment of Sisi’s counterterrorism policy; the page does not specify 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The description attributes the military campaign and associated policy effects to President Sisi.","limitations":["The event page does not provide quantitative security outcomes or a 2023-specific assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b51ab43ff605f779","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A Brookings commentary characterizes Sisi’s regime as highly repressive, links his rise to the 2013 military coup and massacre of Muslim Brotherhood supporters, and states that repression escalated after March 2015 across nearly every metric; it also describes tens of thousands of prisoners and inhuman detention conditions.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical context for 2023; published in 2017 and not a 2023 assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The author attributes the repression and detention system to the Sisi regime.","limitations":["Some claims are the author’s synthesis and are not independently quantified in the supplied units."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a4701a588ed101b3","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A Brookings analysis reports that Egypt’s constitution guarantees freedom of religion on paper, but blasphemy is harshly punished; it states that Sisi attended Christmas Eve Mass and publicly emphasized Egyptian unity, while Christian representation remained low, proactive protection was inadequate, anti-Coptic violence persisted, and perpetrators of earlier abuses and church attacks had not been fully brought to justice or reconstructed.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","4B.7","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical evidence preceding 2023; the analysis was published in 2016.","ruler_attribution":"The analysis attributes the public inclusion rhetoric and government practices to President Sisi and his government.","limitations":["No 2023-specific incident or outcome is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e26ef14ad0fe0ec1","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"As of 28 February 2023, the World Bank’s Egypt portfolio supported human development; social protection and jobs; health, nutrition and population; environment, agriculture and food; water; and urban development, supplemented by advisory and analytical services.","question_ids":["5B.6","6B.2","6B.6","6B.9","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly fits 2023 portfolio status, though it describes World Bank-supported operations rather than solely Egyptian government action.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the portfolio to World Bank support for Egypt’s development efforts; it does not establish that Sisi personally directed each operation.","limitations":["No amounts, execution rates, beneficiaries, or measured outcomes are provided in the supplied unit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cc033106fd134fc6","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"On the tenth anniversary of the Rabaa massacre, Amnesty reported that more than 900 people were killed in the 2013 dispersal, no official had been held accountable, tens of thousands were arrested, critics remained in prolonged pretrial detention, and authorities continued using counterterrorism laws, mass trials, death sentences, censorship, torture, enforced disappearance, and arbitrary detention.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 period as a 14 August 2023 retrospective on continuing conditions.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty attributes the continuing policies and impunity to Egyptian authorities and states that Sisi ratified a 2018 immunity law for senior military leaders.","limitations":["The source is an advocacy organization’s assessment and includes cumulative conditions over the decade, not only events occurring in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f78490c615d22771","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"SIPRI reported that Egypt was the world’s seventh-largest arms importer in 2019–2023; its imports included more than 20 combat aircraft and 10 major warships intended to increase military reach.","question_ids":["2B.8","8B.3","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers the 2019–2023 period and therefore includes 2023, but reports five-year transfers rather than 2023-only procurement decisions.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes Egypt’s military-import profile to the Egyptian state; it does not identify Sisi’s personal procurement decisions.","limitations":["SIPRI measures volume of deliveries, not financial value, and does not establish defensive necessity, abuse, corruption, or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The UN Human Rights Committee’s 20 March 2023 concluding observations welcomed Egypt’s National Human Rights Strategy, women’s empowerment strategy, anti-trafficking and anti-corruption strategies, and other legislative or institutional measures, while also noting concerns about the independence and effectiveness of the National Council for Human Rights and the persistence of corruption.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","5B.5","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly fits 2023 because the observations were adopted on 20 March 2023 and assess measures during the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee addresses the Egyptian state; the supplied units do not establish which measures were personally directed by Sisi.","limitations":["The document is supplied as garbled UTF-16 HTML; the extracted text is readable but formatting and some characters are corrupted."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The UN Human Rights Committee found insufficient safeguards for the National Council for Human Rights’ independence and effective implementation of its recommendations, and reported pervasive corruption, limited information on anti-corruption effectiveness, and inadequate independence, transparency, effectiveness, and accountability of the Administrative Control Authority.","question_ids":["3B.4","5B.5","5B.7","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly fits the Committee’s 2023 observations, while describing institutional conditions accumulated during the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egyptian state institutions; they do not make a personal attribution to Sisi beyond presidential control of relevant institutions elsewhere in the document.","limitations":["The Committee reports concerns and information gaps rather than a final judicial finding of individual responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported continuing discrimination, stigmatization, harassment, and violence against people based on sexual orientation or gender identity; it also found that emergency powers and communicable-disease legislation enabled restrictions on assembly, military-court jurisdiction over civilians, indefinite detention with little judicial review, and suppression of expression.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.7","4B.3","4B.9","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations, though the cited laws and practices predate 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern the Egyptian government and state legislation; the supplied units do not attribute each measure personally to Sisi.","limitations":["The Committee’s findings cover the reporting period and legal framework rather than isolating individual 2023 orders."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that broad counterterrorism definitions and expanded death-penalty offenses were used with restrictive laws to silence peaceful protesters, lawyers, journalists, political opponents, and human-rights defenders; thousands were reportedly listed as terrorists without hearings or due process, with travel bans, asset freezes, or automatic dismissal.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 Committee observations; the laws date from 2015 and their reported use spans multiple years.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egyptian authorities and laws enacted under Sisi’s presidency; no individual order is identified.","limitations":["The Committee uses reported information and does not quantify the full affected population."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":14,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that women’s-violence legislation and institutions had significant gaps; domestic violence and marital rape were not explicitly criminalized, honor-crime leniency remained, reporting had not increased, complainants faced intimidation and revictimization, and female-genital-mutilation prevalence had declined among younger women but remained widespread and underreported, especially in marginalized and rural communities.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations, with outcomes and legal conditions accumulated before and through the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee assesses Egyptian legislation and state implementation; it does not assign personal responsibility to Sisi for each gap.","limitations":["The supplied text reports trends without a single national prevalence figure or 2023 budget allocation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":19,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported widespread incommunicado detention and enforced disappearances, severe overcrowding and poor prison conditions, denial of healthcare and visits, solitary confinement, deaths in custody, lack of independent investigations, and restricted independent monitoring access.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.10","6B.2","6B.6","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations, though the reported practices span the reporting period rather than one dated 2023 event.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee attributes the reported practices to Egyptian security, prison, judicial, and state institutions.","limitations":["Most findings are based on reported information; supplied units do not provide a complete official detention census."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":22,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"The Committee found frequent arbitrary detention, repeated renewal of pretrial cases through ‘rotation,’ punitive use against dissenters, journalists, defenders and opponents, and prolonged pretrial detention contributing to overcrowding and an absence of public detention records.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations, with the practice described as ongoing and systemic.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egyptian security and judicial authorities under the state party.","limitations":["The Committee does not identify individual decision-makers for the reported detention practices."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":25,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that constitutional amendments allowing the President to appoint heads of judicial bodies and the prosecutor compromised judicial independence, while politically motivated cases, prolonged pretrial detention, and fair-trial violations affected critics and opponents.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.4","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations; the constitutional amendments date from 2019 but remained operative in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee specifically describes presidential appointment authority and the President-headed Supreme Council for Judicial Bodies.","limitations":["The finding concerns institutional design and reported cases, not a particular 2023 appointment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":29,"end_unit":32,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported that restrictive laws were used against journalists, independent media, social-media users, women and girls, peaceful protesters, activists, and civil-society organizations; it cited website blocking, detention, broad monitoring and dissolution powers, asset freezes, travel bans, mass arrests, and excessive force with no adequate accountability.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations, while covering laws and practices adopted over several years.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee attributes these practices to Egyptian authorities and executive-controlled regulatory institutions.","limitations":["The supplied units summarize reported patterns and do not identify a single 2023 enforcement action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":33,"end_unit":35,"fact_summary":"The Committee welcomed Egypt’s anti-trafficking measures and national referral mechanism but found that the mechanism was not fully operational and underused; trafficking remained prevalent, including labor and sexual exploitation, child trafficking, and exploitation of migrant women workers.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations; the underlying anti-trafficking law dates from 2010 and implementation is assessed during the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egyptian state anti-trafficking institutions.","limitations":["No 2023 prevalence estimate or resource allocation is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":35,"end_unit":37,"fact_summary":"The Committee acknowledged that Egypt hosted significant numbers of refugees and asylum-seekers but reported no adequate asylum framework, border detention without access to procedures, alleged collective expulsions violating non-refoulement, disappearances after deportation, and substandard immigration detention conditions.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations, with reported practices during the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern the Egyptian state’s border, asylum, and detention authorities.","limitations":["The supplied units do not provide refugee totals or identify individual orders."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":37,"end_unit":40,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported that emergency and military courts had expanded jurisdiction, thousands of critics and opponents including children were tried in proceedings lacking fair-trial safeguards, death sentences were frequent and often unappealable, and military judges were appointed through the Defence Ministry and military chain of command.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations; the legal framework and practices span the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee identifies presidentially influenced judicial structures and military-chain appointments but does not assign each case personally to Sisi.","limitations":["The finding is institutional and cumulative rather than a 2023 case count."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":43,"end_unit":45,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that religious and belief minorities, including Copts, Shia Muslims, Jehovah’s Witnesses, Baha’is and atheists, faced restrictions on worship and burial, blasphemy prosecutions, sectarian attacks with impunity, and exclusion from official recognition; conscientious objectors lacked a lawful alternative-service route.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.7","4B.7","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations, though the cited restrictions and attacks span prior years.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egyptian law and state protection practices.","limitations":["No specific 2023 attack or presidential statement is identified."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":47,"end_unit":49,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that Egypt’s assembly law imposed undue restrictions, allowed protest bans without justification, enabled disproportionate force and heavy criminal sanctions, and was associated with mass arrests and detention; it also found that the civil-society law restricted registration, funding and operations and enabled harassment, investigations, detention, travel bans and asset freezes.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations; the laws date from 2013 and 2019 but remained operative in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee attributes the framework and enforcement to the Egyptian state.","limitations":["The source does not provide a 2023 protest count or specify Sisi’s individual role in each enforcement action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0edb13d328c1b9a","start_unit":51,"end_unit":52,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that political parties could be denied registration or dissolved on broadly defined national-security or national-unity grounds, religious parties were prohibited, and the Political Parties Commission lacked adequate guarantees of judicial independence.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 observations; the cited legal framework predates but remained applicable during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egypt’s party-law and institutional framework.","limitations":["No specific 2023 party registration or dissolution decision is identified."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-d71e38e35220bcd6","SRC-0c6789ed26a74ebd","SRC-8febc9cc1c3fd83c"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied sources concern periods before or after 2023; their facts are retained only where they provide material historical context for assessing the 2023 ruler-period.","The supplied UN document is garbled UTF-16 extracted HTML, although the substantive cited units are interpretable.","No supplied document provides a reliable 2023-specific fact materially addressing chapter 1B nuclear or other catastrophic-risk questions."]}
